paper.title: LLMs as Search Engine Components and Users: Infrastructural Adaptations to a Dual Transformation
paper.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are inducing a dual transformation in search engines: an internal transformation of search architectures and an external transformation of search traffic dynamics. As part of the internal transformation, LLMs are integrated into search engine pipelines as retrievers, re-rankers, query rewriters, and orchestrators [6]. While yielding strong effectiveness gains, these components introduce substantial computational and infrastructural costs, making search compute-bound and harder to scale. Moreover, LLM-based modules are sensitive to distributional shifts, noisy inputs [6], increasing system performance dependence on data quality, input distributions, and upstream design choices. At the same time, LLMs are emerging as autonomous users of search engines [2, 5], inducing an external transformation of search traffic. Their queries differ from human queries in structure, reformulation patterns, volume, and generation speed, and may be generated iteratively as part of multi-step reasoning processes. However, most search engine components remain optimised for human search behaviours.
